title: Why Pen Caps Have a Tiny Hole
description:
Why do pen caps have a tiny hole? It isn't for the ink. People chew caps, and now and then someone breathes one in by accident, and a smooth cap can plug an airway like a cork. So the safety standard ISO 11540 says caps on pens that kids might use need a way for air to get through: at least 8 litres of air a minute. That's why the hole is there, or the cap is made too big to swallow. The hole in the side of the pen has a different job: it lets air in so the ink keeps flowing.

Still chewing yours?
